title: DSI-2 — Scope-Level Sub-Scope Search Delivery
summary: include eligible documents from visibly hosted sub-scopes in one parent-scope search index with exact collection identity, active-route navigation, and compact collection context
content_html:
DSI-2 — Scope-Level Sub-Scope Search Delivery

Status

DSI-2.0 is complete and parked for review. No implementation is approved. Production code, tests, combined-corpus search output, public projections, and browser presentation remain unchanged pending approval to begin DSI-2.1.

The current system deliberately excludes sub-scope documents from parent Index, Recent, and Search. This delivery supersedes that decision for Search only. Parent Index and Recent remain separate unless another delivery explicitly changes them.

Settled Product Boundary

The main Docs Viewer search represents the complete visible documentation experience for its active parent scope. One scope-level index should therefore contain:

  • eligible ordinary parent documents; and
  • eligible documents from each registered sub-scope placed by an eligible docs_subscope report host in that scope.

All records participate in one query and one relevance order. Corpus statistics used by Docs Viewer Search Relevance cover the same combined scope corpus.

The title search inside a sub-scope report remains a quick filter over that report's current list. It does not become a second full-text engine. DSI-2 does not generate independent sub-scope search indexes or merge separately queried indexes in the browser.

Identity, Navigation, And Presentation

A sub-scope search record retains exact semantic identity {scope, sub_scope, doc_id}. Its report-host placement is also explicit so the browser can open the document through the correct active route. Titles, filenames, currently selected reports, and displayed UI state must not be used to infer any part of the target.

The same Analysis search projection is consumed by local Manage and public /analysis/, which require different route bases. Ordinary document-to-document links already use the shared active-route resolver, including exact subdoc and fragment preservation; DSI-2 does not introduce another link-resolution system. Search data must carry the structured parent report-host plus child target needed by that existing resolver rather than treating one stored public or Manage href as universal. The resolver then constructs the canonical parent report URL for the active route and preserves the exact child as subdoc.

Sub-scope result context should follow the existing compact metadata pattern. Beneath the document title, display update date plus the configured collection/report title, for example 2026-07-27 • Concepts. Keep exact sub_scope, report-host identity, and configured collection title as separate data; do not overload parent_title or make collection context searchable merely because it is displayed.

Membership And Publication

Include only a registered sub-scope with one unambiguous eligible report-host placement. Include only child documents present in the corresponding eligible collection product. Stop rather than guess if placement, collection identity, or document identity is ambiguous.

For public Analysis, the combined index must derive membership from the same accepted public report hosts, public manifests, and public by-ID projections used by the existing document-location boundary. It must not expose vocabulary from unpublished, non-publishable, Manage-only, hidden, orphaned, or unplaced child documents. Local and external-local scopes use their corresponding working collection products without weakening exact identity.

The parent report host remains an ordinary parent result in its own right. Child content is indexed once under its exact sub-scope identity. Collection membership neither boosts nor penalises relevance.

Build And Rebuild Direction

Every eligible parent and child document uses the same configured title, heading, body, and code extraction and tokenizer policy when its scope adopts full text. Structural collection fields remain display and navigation metadata only.

The combined posting lists remain one atomic scope artifact. A search-relevant sub-scope source or membership change must rebuild the complete parent-scope search index, while its document-payload build may remain collection-targeted. The current sub-scope write path reports search mode none; DSI-2 must replace that behavior without broadening document rebuilding.

Delivery Steps

DSI-2.0 — Composition And Route Readiness

  • [x] Confirm the exact parent and sub-scope source/projection membership owners for repository, public, and external-local scopes.
  • [x] Reuse the existing exact document-location/report-host association and active-route URL resolver used by ordinary document-to-document links; do not create a second route mechanism or title-based or selected-report inference.
  • [x] Confirm the smallest additive search-record target needed to preserve {scope, sub_scope, doc_id} plus one unambiguous report-host placement across Manage and public routes.
  • [x] Inspect actual ID uniqueness across parent and child collections; stop rather than assume doc_id alone is scope-wide unique.
  • [x] Identify the watcher and write-service changes required for a sub-scope change to rebuild only the atomic parent search artifact.
  • [x] Measure current and proposed Analysis parent/sub-scope record counts and raw payload shape without changing the generated or public index.
  • [x] Present exact proposed files and a rough production/test diff estimate.

Gate: Review membership, structured navigation target, schema compatibility, rebuild ownership, public exclusion evidence, payload estimate, and proposed files before implementation.

Record: Completed 2026-08-14. docs_scopes.json owns registered parent/sub-scope identity and repository versus external-local locations. build_search.py owns the atomic parent index. The sub-scope builder's working manifest.json and by-ID family are the eligible collection product; for a public-capable collection that manifest is already the public-safe publishable subset, while manage-manifest.json remains outside Search membership. Eligible parent report hosts are the already-filtered parent search records carrying one validated docs_subscope descriptor. Analysis additionally requires access: public; its explicit Publish copies the accepted working search and prepared sub-scope products to the public destinations. The existing exact report-host association in docs_document_location.py and public projection in docs_document_location_projection.py remain the placement owners.

The active-route seam is the existing buildViewerUrl/route-workflow path, which already selects the current Manage or public base and preserves report parameters. The smallest additive child record keeps scope in the index header and doc_id in the existing id, then adds exact sub_scope, report_doc_id, and display-only collection_title. The existing href can remain for v2 compatibility but is not navigation authority; the result path must construct the active parent URL from report_doc_id and pass the child as subdoc. display_meta remains the compact rendered string. parent_title is not overloaded and collection context emits no postings. Uniqueness and deterministic ordering must use the complete target rather than doc_id alone.

Current eligible counts are Studio 241 parent plus 2 default children, Analysis 17 parent plus 249 children, and external-local dotlineform 9 parent plus 241 projects children. Each registered collection has one eligible host and the inspected data has no parent/child or child/child ID collision, but the schema will not rely on that contingent fact. Notes and Processing have no registered sub-scope and remain unchanged. Analysis's 249 children are 248 Concepts and 1 Works. Four Manage-visible publishable: false children are absent from both working/public manifests and public by-ID files. The current public document-location projection already contains the intended 266 exact records, providing an independent membership and route cross-check.

The current Analysis index is 17 records, 66 terms, and 10,538 raw bytes. An in-memory additive metadata-only projection using the accepted fields and current public-safe collection products is 266 records, 569 terms, and approximately 140,949 raw bytes: +249 records and +130,411 bytes. Parent row shapes remain unchanged; child rows add only sub_scope, report_doc_id, and collection_title to the current identity, title, route, update, and display fields. No generated or public file was written to obtain this estimate.

The write-service change belongs in perform_sub_scope_source_write_and_rebuild: keep the child Docs build collection-confined, then run one complete parent Search build and include that step in rollback recovery. The low-level child-only rebuild remains available for sub-scope lifecycle creation, which already performs the correctly ordered parent Docs/Search rebuild after creating the report host, and for projection-only lineage refreshes. The live watcher needs the same child-Docs-then-parent-Search sequence. Parent host or configuration changes continue through their existing parent/lifecycle rebuild owners. Public Delete cleanup must remove one exact child search target and remap postings without deleting a same-ID target in another collection. The public document-location projection must ignore structured child search rows as parent inputs so it continues to emit one location per exact target rather than expand children twice.

Proposed production files are docs-viewer/build/build_search.py, docs-viewer/services/docs_document_location.py, docs-viewer/services/docs_document_location_projection.py, docs-viewer/services/docs_public_delete_cleanup.py, docs-viewer/services/docs_write_rebuild.py, docs-viewer/services/docs_live_rebuild_watcher.py, site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-search.js, site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-search-controller.js, and site/docs-viewer/runtime/js/shared/docs-viewer-route-workflow.js. Proposed focused test files are docs-viewer/tests/python/test_build_search_python.py, test_build_document_locations.py, test_docs_public_delete_cleanup.py, test_docs_write_rebuild.py, test_docs_live_rebuild_watcher.py, test_docs_import_sub_scope.py, test_docs_management_subscope_delete.py, and docs-viewer/tests/js/docs_viewer_search_v2_contract.mjs. The expected review shape is roughly 250-350 production lines and 250-400 focused test lines across those existing owners, with no new framework, browser test, independent child index, route resolver, or scope-name search branch. Material expansion beyond that shape is a stop condition.

DSI-2.1 should regenerate the affected working indexes only after its focused builder, exclusion, cleanup, and rebuild evidence passes. The tracked Analysis public index remains behind an explicit Publish delta review; DSI-2.0 did not publish it. The routine Docs watcher regenerated this delivery record's Studio by-ID, tree, Recent, and existing parent-only search projections after the status edit; it did not change a search schema, corpus-composition owner, or public file. Gate outcome: ready for DSI-2.1 implementation review, with DSI-2.2 browser presentation and navigation intentionally not started.

DSI-2.1 — Combined Scope Index

  • [ ] Extend the shared builder to emit one deterministic scope corpus containing eligible parent and visibly hosted sub-scope documents.
  • [ ] Retain exact collection identity, route placement, configured display context, and one result per exact document target.
  • [ ] Apply the same field extraction and tokenizer to parent and child content without a scope-name or sub-scope-name branch.
  • [ ] Make search-relevant child writes and membership changes rebuild the complete parent-scope index.
  • [ ] Prove excluded child documents contribute neither identities nor terms, especially in the public Analysis projection.

Gate: Present generated contract, combined-corpus counts, exact exclusion evidence, rebuild behavior, payload delta, and non-Analysis scope comparison. Stop before browser presentation.

DSI-2.2 — Exact Result Navigation And Context

  • [ ] Make the shared search result path pass the structured parent report-host plus child target to the existing active-route resolver for parent and child results.
  • [ ] Preserve ordinary parent navigation and query/history behavior.
  • [ ] Show configured collection/report context beneath child titles using the existing compact result metadata pattern.
  • [ ] Leave visual and interaction acceptance to the user; do not add or run a browser check unless explicitly requested.

Gate: Stop for direct user feedback on mixed parent/child results and public versus Manage navigation before code review.

DSI-2.3 — Code Review And Closeout

  • [ ] Review builder, membership, publication, schema, routing, write/rebuild, result presentation, tests, documentation, and generated projections.
  • [ ] Check specifically for hidden vocabulary leakage, ambiguous placement, inferred identity, parent-route regressions, stale child postings, duplicated search artifacts, and collection-based rank drift.
  • [ ] Transfer settled behavior to durable Search and Search Index documents while retaining delivery evidence here.
  • [ ] Run only the focused accepted checks and stop for explicit closeout approval.

Gate: Present review findings, resolutions, final scope, and remaining limitations. Stop for explicit closeout approval.

Boundaries

DSI-2 changes Search corpus composition only. It does not merge sub-scope documents into the parent tree or Recent list, replace report-local title filtering, add cross-scope search, create independent child indexes, change relevance scoring, change Catalogue Search, or publish Analysis full text before its separate adoption gate.
